newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus limits rallies, bans national symbols.
newsitem.headline: Belarus limits rallies, bans national symbols.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko ordered restrictions on political rallies on Thursday and banned his opponents from using post-independence national symbols, which he has scrapped in favour of old Soviet ones.

"The holding of meetings and rallies, demonstrations and pickets is banned if their aim is to violate the existing constitutional system, pro-war propaganda or social, ethnic, religious or racial hatred," the decree read.
Acording to the decree, organisers must apply for permission to hold gatherings in the capital Minsk 15 days in advance to the city authorities.
Last weekend some 5,000 demonstrators gathered in central Minsk to protest agaist Lukashenko's pro-Russian policies.
Opposition spokesmen said the decree would not stop them from holding mass rallies against Lukashenko and his policies.

"This shows that the authorities fear mass protests in Belarus, which are due in the coming months," Lyavon Barshchevski, leader of opposition Belarussian Popular Front, told Reuters. "But they will not stop the political spring in Belarus and will not intimidate us."

Last April, Lukashenko jailed 200 people for taking part in a rally marking the anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster across the border in Ukraine. He also banned all political rallies during the harvest.

The U.S. State Department accused Belarus last week of failing to uphold democracy and human rights and announced it was halting all U.S. aid to the country of 10 million. It also said that freedom of assembly and expression has been challenged in Belarus under Lukashenko's rule.
Foreign Minister Ivan Antonovich said on Thursday the decree was necessary.

"We must establish order into the organisation of demonstrations because even Saint Valentine's Day (February 14) was turned into political slogans and calls to destroy the constitutitonal order," Antonovich told a news conference.
The decree also bans use at rallies of those national symbols which Lukashenko scrapped in 1995, four years after they were introduced following the break-up of the Soviet Union.

Last November Lukashenko, who will discuss closer integration with Russia in talks with President Boris Yeltsin in Moscow on Friday, took broad powers and rewrote the former Soviet republic's constitution. Opposition and human rights activists accused him of increasingly authoritarian rule.

According to the decree, taking part in a banned rally can lead to 15 days in jail or a fine of up to $750. The average monthly wage in Belarus is about $50. For a second offence, the fine will be up to $1,500.
For using non-official symbols, fines stand at between $50 and $500.
